name_reason: Current name follows the convention exactly: data_fd2_ prefix (game global), battle_ domain (battle core table), tile_attr_def_modifier_table descriptor correctly reflects both purpose (per-tile-attribute defense percent modifier) and data type (_table = array). No Ghidra address residue; the only numerics are the array dimension. All 5 reader xref sites confirm the semantics.
purpose: Per-tile-attribute defense percent modifier table: indexed by terrain attribute id (0..5), gives the signed percentage applied to a unit's DP when standing on that terrain.
logic_summary: const int[6] read-only lookup table. Readers fetch tile_attr via fd2_read_tile_attribute_at_pos, then compute effective_DP = DP + (table[tile_attr] * DP) / 100 (signed IDIV by 100). Sibling AP/MV table at 0x51A12 (data_fd2_battle_tile_attr_mv_modifier_table); the next symbol at 0x51A42 bounds this table at exactly 6 elements / 24 bytes. The HUD renderer also displays the raw value directly as the DEF row via fd2_render_signed_modifier_with_icon.
element_semantics: Each element is a signed 32-bit percentage DEF modifier for one terrain attribute id (index 0..5). Values = { 0, 0, 10, 10, -5, 0 }; e.g. terrain ids 2/3 grant +10% DP, terrain id 4 imposes a -5% DP penalty, ids 0/1/5 are neutral.
comment_original_issue: The src block was already accurate, but the line immediately above the declaration read '/* Non-const for the same reason as the MV sibling above. */' while the symbol is (correctly) declared 'const int32'. That stale/contradictory note was misleading: the table has zero game-side write xrefs, so const is correct. Replaced the note with a correct const justification.
notes: 5 reader xref sites (4 distinct functions; fd2_ai_score_physical_attack references it twice): fd2_execute_attack_damage_calculation @ 0x1edec, fd2_calculate_combat_hit_outcome @ 0x2a0c5, fd2_ai_score_physical_attack @ 0x14413/0x14573, fd2_render_terrain_info_hud_panel @ 0x1adf1. All are READ-only; zero writers => const. Ghidra symbol name and datatype (int[6]) already match the C definition. Ghidra plate was empty (null) so a concise ASCII plate was created reflecting the src conclusion.
